title: Module 9 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

o: Measures the same participants under both conditions
items.why: Each person serves as his or her own comparison, which removes stable individual differences from the error.

o: Pairs participants on a relevant variable and assigns one of each pair to each condition
items.why: Matched pairs are treated like repeated measures because each pair's scores are related.

items.q: For a related-samples t test, the analysis is performed on
o: The raw scores of each group separately
The sums of squares between groups
items.why: The test reduces two scores per person to one difference score and runs a one-sample t on those differences.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for a related-samples t test are
o: n minus 1, where n is the number of pairs or difference scores
items.why: df depends on the number of difference scores.

items.q: The null hypothesis for a related-samples t is
o: The mean difference in the population is zero
The two sample means are equal

items.q: A major advantage of a related-samples design is
o: It removes individual differences from the error term, which often increases power
items.why: People differ in stable ways. Comparing each person with himself or herself cancels that variability.

items.q: A potential problem with repeated measures is
o: Order effects such as practice or fatigue
items.why: Counterbalancing the order of conditions addresses this threat.

items.q: Cohen's d for a related-samples t is commonly computed as
o: Mean difference divided by the SD of the difference scores
Mean difference divided by the standard error
Mean difference divided by the sample mean
items.why: It expresses the average change in units of the standard deviation of the changes.

items.q: The assumption of independence for an independent-measures t means
o: Each score is unrelated to every other score
The two groups are the same size
items.why: A violation, such as measuring the same people twice, requires a different test.

items.q: A confidence interval for the mean difference that does not include zero indicates that
o: A two-tailed test at the matching alpha would reject the null
items.why: Zero is not a plausible value for the true difference.
